sn55.21:1.4: _Byūha_ (cul-de-sac”) is defined in the Vinaya: “one departs the same way one enters” ([pli-tv-bi-vb-pc14:2.1.8]()).
sn55.21:1.13: This relates to the commonly-held idea in modern Theravada that rebirth is determined by one’s “last mind-moment”. This idea is incorrect on a number of grounds. First, there’s no such thing as “mind moments” in early Buddhism. Second, rebirth is determined not by “thought” (_citta_) but by “deed” (_kamma_). So it would only apply in the case of someone who was actually committing good or bad kamma at the time of death, which most people are not. Finally, what normally prevails at the time of death is habitual _kamma_ (like keeping precepts every day) or very strong _kamma_ (such as attaining _jhāna_).
sn55.21:3.2: There is a parallel for this simile at [sn42.6:7.1]().
